correctness.rationale: The three-survivor intersection criterion is exact. A heavy coordinate occurs in at most one codeword. For n>=6 any two exceptional words intersect in at least 2n-8>=4, giving the five-or-four bounds; at n=5 compatible exceptional doubled-coordinate pairs must be disjoint, yielding at most two exceptions. The four constants plus exceptions attain each case. Labeled maximizers are enumerated independently by the heavy-exception combinatorial counts 12*24=288, 4*144+6*22=708, 4*4=16, and 1, with the specific 144 and 22 completions derived algebraically in RESULT.md. The S4 orbit counts 14,46,2,1 follow by Burnside from fixed counts exhaustively obtained by a complete increasing-index compatibility-mask recursion. verify.py also checks all three-element shadows independently, redoes counts from exceptional/heavy categories, and uses no floating-point optimizer. No finite computation is used to infer the infinite-n size formula.

value.rationale: Three-survivor multiset correction is a natural near-extremal channel analyzed explicitly in arXiv:2601.05636. At q=4 its available general numerical bound leaves a substantial gap. The theorem determines the entire optimal-cardinality function for all n>=5, its two sharp finite-length transitions, every maximum code at the four exceptional lengths, and their structural symmetry classes, including 46 distinct length-six alphabet orbits. This is a motivated natural finite/infinite classification with value beyond an incidental single arithmetic computation; no wider code-improvement claim is made.
